rows.stem: The string of a flying kite is tied to a point on the ground. The length of the string between the kite and the point on the ground is 80 m. The string makes an angle of \(30^\circ\) with the ground. The height of the kite above the ground is :
rows.solution:
The string, the vertical height of the kite and the ground form a right triangle with the string as hypotenuse. Let h be the height.

\(\sin 30^\circ = \dfrac{h}{80}\), so \(h = 80 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 40\) m.

This is option (B) 40 m.

rows.stem: Shown in the given figure is a circle with centre O. The area of the minor sector is \(7\,\text{cm}^2\). Area of circle is :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - circle with centre O and radii OS and OT; the 30 degree angle of the minor sector SOT is marked only in the drawing. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
The minor sector SOT has a central angle of \(30^\circ\), which is \(\dfrac{30}{360} = \dfrac{1}{12}\) of the whole circle.

So \(\dfrac{1}{12} \times\) area of circle \(= 7\), and the area of the circle \(= 7 \times 12 = 84\ \text{cm}^2\).

This is option (C) \(84\,\text{cm}^2\).

rows.stem: In the given figure, O is the centre of circle. XYZ is an arc of the circle subtending an angle of \(45^\circ\) at the centre. If the radius of the circle is 32 cm, then the length of the arc XYZ is :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - circle with centre O, radii OX and OZ and the 45 degree angle at O, Y on the arc; the stem states the angle and the radius. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
Length of the arc \(= \dfrac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times 2\pi r = \dfrac{45}{360} \times 2\pi \times 32 = \dfrac{1}{8} \times 64\pi = 8\pi\) cm.

This is option (B) \(8\pi\) cm.

rows.subtopic: Volume of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: The radius of a sphere (in cm) whose volume is \(36\pi\,\text{cm}^3\), is :
rows.solution:
\(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = 36\pi\) gives \(r^3 = \dfrac{36 \times 3}{4} = 27\), so \(r = 3\) cm.

This is option (A) \(3\).

rows.stem: Do the points P \((1, 0)\), Q \((-5, 0)\) and R \((-2, 5)\) form a triangle ? If so, name the type of triangle formed.
rows.solution:
By the distance formula:

\(PQ = \sqrt{(-5 - 1)^2 + (0 - 0)^2} = \sqrt{36} = 6\)

\(QR = \sqrt{(-2 + 5)^2 + (5 - 0)^2} = \sqrt{9 + 25} = \sqrt{34} \approx 5.83\)

\(PR = \sqrt{(-2 - 1)^2 + (5 - 0)^2} = \sqrt{9 + 25} = \sqrt{34} \approx 5.83\)

The sum of any two sides is greater than the third (the longest side is 6, and \(2\sqrt{34} \approx 11.66 > 6\)), so the points are not collinear and P, Q and R form a triangle.

\(QR = PR\), so the triangle is isosceles. (It is not right-angled, since \(34 + 34 = 68 \neq 36\).)

rows.subtopic: Forming a Quadratic Polynomial from its Zeroes
rows.stem: Find a quadratic polynomial whose zeroes are \(\left(5 - 2\sqrt{3}\right)\) and \(\left(5 + 2\sqrt{3}\right)\).
rows.solution:
Let \(\alpha = 5 - 2\sqrt{3}\) and \(\beta = 5 + 2\sqrt{3}\).

\(\alpha + \beta = 10\) and \(\alpha\beta = 5^2 - (2\sqrt{3})^2 = 25 - 12 = 13\).

A quadratic polynomial with these zeroes is \(x^2 - (\alpha + \beta)x + \alpha\beta\), that is \(x^2 - 10x + 13\) (or any non-zero constant multiple of it).

rows.subtopic: Surface Area of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: A right circular cylinder and a right circular cone have equal bases and equal heights. If their curved surface areas are in the ratio 8 : 5, then find the ratio between the radius of their bases to their height.
rows.solution:
Let r be the common radius and h the common height, and let \(l = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2}\) be the slant height of the cone.

Curved surface area of the cylinder \(= 2\pi rh\), and of the cone \(= \pi rl\). So

\(\dfrac{2\pi rh}{\pi rl} = \dfrac{8}{5}\), that is \(\dfrac{2h}{\sqrt{r^2 + h^2}} = \dfrac{8}{5}\).

\(10h = 8\sqrt{r^2 + h^2}\). Squaring: \(100h^2 = 64r^2 + 64h^2\), so \(36h^2 = 64r^2\).

\(\dfrac{r^2}{h^2} = \dfrac{36}{64}\), so \(\dfrac{r}{h} = \dfrac{6}{8} = \dfrac{3}{4}\).

The ratio of the radius to the height is \(3 : 4\).

rows.subtopic: Probability with Cards, Dice and Coins
rows.stem:
Two different coins are tossed simultaneously. What is the probability of getting :

(i) at least one head ?

(ii) at most one tail ?

(iii) a head and a tail ?
rows.solution:
Tossing two coins gives 4 equally likely outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT.

(i) At least one head: HH, HT, TH, that is 3 outcomes. \(P = \dfrac{3}{4}\).

(ii) At most one tail (no tail or one tail): HH, HT, TH, that is 3 outcomes. \(P = \dfrac{3}{4}\).

(iii) A head and a tail: HT, TH, that is 2 outcomes. \(P = \dfrac{2}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

rows.stem:
The marks obtained by 80 students of class X in a mock test of Mathematics are given below in the table. Find **median** and the **mode** of the data :

| Marks | Number of Students |
|---|---|
| 0 and above | 80 |
| 10 and above | 77 |
| 20 and above | 72 |
| 30 and above | 65 |
| 40 and above | 55 |
| 50 and above | 43 |
| 60 and above | 28 |
| 70 and above | 16 |
| 80 and above | 10 |
| 90 and above | 8 |
| 100 and above | 0 |
rows.solution:
Turn the "and above" (more than type) table into class frequencies: each class frequency is the difference between consecutive counts, for example \(80 - 77 = 3\) students scored in 0-10.

| Marks | \(f\) | \(cf\) |
|---|---|---|
| 0-10 | 3 | 3 |
| 10-20 | 5 | 8 |
| 20-30 | 7 | 15 |
| 30-40 | 10 | 25 |
| 40-50 | 12 | 37 |
| 50-60 | 15 | 52 |
| 60-70 | 12 | 64 |
| 70-80 | 6 | 70 |
| 80-90 | 2 | 72 |
| 90-100 | 8 | 80 |
| Total | 80 | |

Median: \(n = 80\), so \(\dfrac{n}{2} = 40\). The first cumulative frequency above 40 is 52, so the median class is 50-60, with \(l = 50\), \(cf = 37\), \(f = 15\) and \(h = 10\).

Median \(= l + \dfrac{\frac{n}{2} - cf}{f} \times h = 50 + \dfrac{40 - 37}{15} \times 10 = 50 + 2 = 52\).

Mode: the highest frequency is 15, so the modal class is 50-60, with \(l = 50\), \(f_1 = 15\), \(f_0 = 12\), \(f_2 = 12\) and \(h = 10\).

Mode \(= l + \dfrac{f_1 - f_0}{2f_1 - f_0 - f_2} \times h = 50 + \dfrac{15 - 12}{30 - 12 - 12} \times 10 = 50 + \dfrac{3}{6} \times 10 = 55\).

The median is 52 marks and the mode is 55 marks.

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.subtopic: Graphical Method and Nature of Solutions
rows.stem: Draw the graph of the pair of linear equations \(x - y + 2 = 0\) and \(4x - y - 4 = 0\). Calculate the area of the triangle formed by the lines so drawn and the \(x\)-axis.
rows.solution:
Points on \(x - y + 2 = 0\), that is \(y = x + 2\):

| \(x\) | \(-2\) | 0 | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(y\) | 0 | 2 | 4 |

Points on \(4x - y - 4 = 0\), that is \(y = 4x - 4\):

| \(x\) | 0 | 1 | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(y\) | \(-4\) | 0 | 4 |

Plot the points and draw the two lines on the same axes. They intersect at \((2, 4)\). The first line meets the x-axis at \((-2, 0)\) and the second at \((1, 0)\).

So the triangle formed by the two lines and the x-axis has vertices \((-2, 0)\), \((1, 0)\) and \((2, 4)\).

Its base along the x-axis is \(1 - (-2) = 3\) units, and its height is the y-coordinate of the vertex \((2, 4)\), that is 4 units.

Area of the triangle \(= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 4 = 6\) square units.
